_: The contact-sheet contract. Swift (ios/App/Shared/SheetSpec.swift) and Java (android/app/src/main/java/app/spotter/dev/SheetSpec.java) each mirror these numbers in code because neither shell can parse a repo file at runtime; tools/ios/sheet-check.mjs and tools/android/sheet-check.mjs compile those mirrors and assert them against this file, so a change here that is not made in both places fails the harness.
__v2: Revised 15 Sept after the first live read. At 200 px cells the reader hedged — 'hands on the mat near the kettlebell' when they are ON the handle — so the cells grew to 270 px and the grid shrank to 4x3, with up to three sheets carrying the same total pixel budget across more of the clip.

frames._: One frame per 2.5 s of video, never fewer than 8 and never more than three full sheets. Times are uniform from edge_inset_s to duration - edge_inset_s, so neither the cold-open logo frame nor the trailing black frame is ever the only look at an exercise.
frames.__min_gap: The generator is allowed half a second of slack, so two neighbouring requests can return the same sync sample. Frames closer together than this are dropped rather than given a duplicate cell — that also keeps the times array strictly ascending, which the server requires.

cell._: Aspect-fit into a fixed box, never cropped: the model has to see what is at the edge of a portrait frame (a kettlebell on the floor, a second dumbbell) and a crop is exactly where that goes missing. Unused box area is black. The orientation is decided from the video's own pixel dimensions with a 5 percent dead band so 1080x1088 does not read as landscape.

grid._: 4 columns by 3 rows, twelve cells to a sheet, up to three sheets per save. Row-major within a sheet and sheet after sheet, so reading order is time order across the whole set. A portrait sheet is exactly cols*cell_w by rows*cell_h — 1080x1440 — which is why the 2 px gutter is drawn INSIDE each cell (a 1 px inset on every side) rather than added between them: two portrait frames of the same person against the same wall merge into one image without a gutter, and the sheet has to stay the size the contract says it is.

label._: The timestamp is the whole point of the labels: the server prompt tells the model to read t0/t1 off them, and the transcript it gets alongside is on the same clock. Bottom-left, because that corner is background in a portrait video far more often than any other.

jpeg._: 0.72 is where JPEG stops paying for itself on video stills. The 600 KB ceiling is the server's per-object limit; one re-encode at 0.62 is allowed rather than a search, because the second pass costs another full encode and the frames are best-effort anyway.

budget._: Hard limits on a save that must never be blocked by them. Past either one, whatever sheets are finished go with the save and the rest are dropped; with none finished the save goes without frames and the server falls back to reading the video with Gemini.

upload._: Object path and MIME the server has to authorise, one per sheet. <n> is 1-based and never exceeds grid.max_sheets.

ingest._: The frames block added to the POST /api/ingest body. Exactly the shape in BRIEF-VCP-A-ADDENDUM.
